prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop landing and documentation homepage comp, 1536×1024 landscape
Primary request: create a second compositional option for the Atlas documentation site, preserving the same 1986 Aegean field-terminal visual world but changing the topology. Make a package constellation map the dominant first-viewport mechanism.
Structure: top navigation with ATLAS, GUIDES, PACKAGES, API, GITHUB. Beneath it, a narrow left dossier column containing the exact statement "Composable, functional Bun/TypeScript building blocks", the exact install command "bun add @wess/atlas", and two actions "START HERE" and "BROWSE PACKAGES". The remaining two-thirds is an interactive-looking celestial package atlas: 19 real module labels arranged as constellations and linked by dependency lines, including CONFIG, DB, SERVER, AUTH, SECURITY, OAUTH, STORAGE, CACHE, REQUEST, CLI, UI, ADMIN, MCP, AI, EDGE, EMAIL, SHARE, SSO, MIGRATE. A quiet band below previews a quick-start code passage and guide chapters.
Style/medium: polished shippable web UI mockup, unmistakably documentation, not a poster. Archaeological survey instruments, Greek star charts, and a late-1980s scientific workstation. Deep Aegean navy, electric cyan technical lines, limestone type, one magenta registration accent, sparse Greek-key rule, subtle CRT phosphor bloom.
Typography: monumental wide uppercase wordmark, highly readable humanist sans for prose, condensed mono for labels and code.
Composition/framing: full browser viewport, asymmetrical 28/72 split, the package constellation is the single focal move; other regions stay quiet and readable.
Constraints: no invented capabilities or metrics, no fake customers, no rounded cards, no bento grid, no generic neon cyberpunk skyline, no gold luxury palette, no Greek column clipart, no glassmorphism, no watermarks, no tiny illegible text.
